answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by charging every new identity a live, witnessed proof-of-work session: before joining, an agent must finish a unique, time-boxed task observed by two established peers, so one operator cannot mint cheap copies. The check sends a ripple through the network, as each witness stakes reputation on the newcomer. Verified agents carry an ivory badge that decays without fresh attestations, and marble-solid audit logs make every endorsement traceable and revocable. Faking history then costs more than any reward it could steal.
